title: Fiber Node Factory
problemStatement: Implement `createFiberNode(tag, type, props)` that initializes a Fiber node with `child: null`, `sibling: null`, `return: null`, `memoizedProps`, and `alternate: null`.
interviewTrap: Confusing `pendingProps` (props being passed to the new render) with `memoizedProps` (props from the last committed render).

testCases.name: Initializes fiber node with null pointers
testCases.testFn: const f = createFiberNode('HostComponent', 'div'); return { child: f.child, sibling: f.sibling, return: f.return };

testCases.name: Assigns type and pending props
testCases.testFn: const f = createFiberNode('HostComponent', 'span', { title: 'hello' }); return f.pendingProps.title;

testCases.name: Sets alternate to null by default (double buffering)
testCases.testFn: const f = createFiberNode('FunctionComponent', () => {}); return f.alternate === null;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: React represents UI as a singly linked list of Fiber nodes (`child`, `sibling`, `return`). Render phase is interruptible and can be paused; commit phase is strictly synchronous.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Fiber Node Structure & Pointers.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Fiber Node Structure & Pointers is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
